title: Rational parabolic subgroups and their fppf right-coset sheaves
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $P,G$ be $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], with a homomorphism $i:P\to G$. On the big fppf site over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fppf-site], define $\mathcal C_i$ to be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the coequalizer of the maps $h_{G\times_kP}\rightrightarrows h_G$, $(g,p)\mapsto g$ and $(g,p)\mapsto g\,i(p)$. On affine test schemes this is the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$. Call $i$ parabolic if it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the scalar extension of $P$ to an algebraic closure using [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and $\mathcal C_i$ is represented by a $k$-scheme $X$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. It is minimal parabolic if it is parabolic and, for every parabolic $j:Q\to G$ and every group homomorphism $f:Q\to P$ with $i\circ f=j$, the morphism $f$ is an isomorphism. Properness of the subgroup means that $i$ is not an isomorphism; minimality itself does not require properness.
